newsitem.title: FINLAND: Credit ratings to affect cost of money in Euro.
newsitem.headline: Credit ratings to affect cost of money in Euro.

text.p: Interest premiums on loans denominated in the Euro are likely to depend on a borrower's credit rating more than under national currencies, Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Thursday.
"Along with a single currency, Euro-countries will share the same central bank interest rates and the same foreign exchange rates," Niinisto told a seminar.
"Euro-denominated market interest rates will also align, but one can assume that the price of money will perhaps start to fluctuate ever more depending on creditworthiness," he said.
Currently, risk premiums on similar investments in different countries vary significantly due to potential currency risk, he noted.
With a single currency, expected with the birth of Economic and Monetary Union in 1999, such interest premiums based on currency risk should more or less disappear.
"Although the currency risk will fade, the market's need for risk differentiation will hardly evaporate but will become ever more focused on credit ratings," Niinisto said.
The impact of credit ratings on effective bond yields can be expected to strengthen, he said.
Yields on government bonds, currently regarded as virtually risk-free investments, might start to include risk premiums.

When the third stage of EMU is born, "sovereign credit ratings may change substantially from the current...and significant yield differences might exist between different countries' government bonds," he said.
"The markets might easily punish an increasing (public sector) financing need and reward a decreasing one," he said.
